assessment.novelty_and_redundancy: R961 identified a current native16 typed-view/live-range plan as a distinct unanswered source question. R962 answers that question. It does not repeat the already integrated GEMM-workspace removal, the existing FP32 prefix-alias work, or the earlier capacity arithmetic; its dedicated-arena versus temporal-remap comparison, parent max table, state and callback boundaries, and >8192 guards are substantive and within budget.

verified_claims.claim: Alloc::take aligns each payload and adds a 256-byte guard; the eight GDN inner takes add 2,048 bytes and the outer shared-region take has its own guard.

With no cache borrow, top-level takes call cudaMalloc and are tracked as separate owners; the SYCL compatibility layer maps each device request to sycl::malloc_device. GDN/QSA/MoE layouts are nested in the one shared-region allocation. Borrowed mode slices its supplied cache range. bytes_needed adds 8 MiB count slack; init separately allocates tok_dev and may allocate a mode-1 identity table.

The prefix, GDN, QSA and compact-MoE arithmetic in report lines 17 and 21-47, including per-take guards and 8 MiB planner slack, matches source. At T=8192, the existing GDN set is 1,180,698,624 B and is the max over QSA and compact MoE.

The current recipe is alias=1/no-prefill-borrow. The 335,544,576 B unused-xn count is an alias-OFF planner overcount and is not current physical savings. Typed BF16 views over FP32 owners do not establish released allocation bytes; short FP32 layout and persistent FP32 state remain constraints.
The report does not claim 16K support, physical 262144 fit, speed, numerical quality, RESTORE, fault qualification, or inference adoption from arithmetic alone.

corrections.correction: The QSA16 shape guard is src/prefill/sycl/qsa_native16.cpp:34-36 (tokens <= 8192), not lines 25-31; 25-31 validate spans/domains. The stated callers are present at 78-79 (norm/RoPE), 124-125 (gate), and 145 (append). The 8192 limit conclusion is correct; fix retrieval anchors in any downstream citation.

The prefix discussion covers ple_emb aliasing and the FP32 bridge, but omits two uses of m.region. Layer-1 batched PLE carves temporary buffers from m.region and bounds its subbatch by m.region_bytes/per_token; for the stated 8192 BF16x2-off case per_token is 142,352 B and its full-chunk conservative bound is 1,166,147,584 B, below the current GDN-sized region. The final float callback may call Prefill::draft_kv, which carves its MTP batch workspace from m.region and sizes B from region_bytes. If that fast path cannot run, generate falls back to mtp.prefill only when the error string is empty. This does not invalidate the current max arithmetic, but a future remap must retain/recompute the PLE scratch bound and preserve or explicitly qualify the MTP callback path.
